title.value: Processing visual ambiguity in fractal patterns: Pareidolia as a sign of creativity
title.justification: The title captures the core subject and objective of the paper, which is about the intersection of visual perception (pareidolia) and creativity, specifically through the exploration of ambiguous fractal patterns.
title.quote: Processing visual ambiguity in fractal patterns: Pareidolia as a sign of creativity

extractions.description: This paper explores the relationship between creativity and pareidolia, the phenomenon of perceiving recognizable forms in ambiguous stimuli such as fractal images. It suggests that more creative individuals report pareidolia across a wider range of image fractal dimensions and it proposes 'divergent perception' as a complementary concept to measure creativity, opening new avenues for studying creative behavior.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily deals with cognitive psychology and the study of creativity, rather than an eco-responsible focus area. It doesn't seem to address topics related to climate change, sustainability, or environmental science directly.
primary_category.quote: Creativity is associated with enhanced pareidolia (i.e., divergent perception)

secondary_categories.justification: As the paper does not engage with subjects typically linked to the environmental, climate, or sustainability fields, no secondary category within the eco-responsible spectrum is applicable.
secondary_categories.quote: Divergent perception constitutes a promising phenomenon for the study of creativity

primary_sub_category.justification: Similar to the primary category, the paper does not delve into any subcategories related to eco-responsibility as it is focused on creativity and perception study.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our results show that the perception of objects in ambiguous fractal stimuli (i.e., pareidolia) occurs more often and more rapidly in creative individuals.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no secondary sub-categories applicable here as the content does not align with any eco-responsible sub-categories given its focus on cognitive sciences.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: These results extend the established body of work on DT by introducing divergent perception as a complementary manifestation of the creative mind.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper fits more naturally into cognitive psychology and creativity studies, exploring how cognitive processes like pareidolia relate to creativity rather than eco-responsible topics.
new_primary_category.quote: Here, in contrast, we examine the perceptual aspect of creativity by asking whether creative individuals are more likely to perceive recognizable forms in ambiguous stimuli –a phenomenon known as pareidolia.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: This sub-category is proposed to encapsulate studies that explore how perception influences creative thinking and understanding in individuals, outside of eco-responsibility categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: A natural approach to exploring inter-individual variability in processing ambiguous images is to exploit pareidolia.
